text:
ajay: Heads-up: eu-west1 GPU pool is showing sustained OOMs and queue backlog. Dashboards -> 90% GPU util, node restarts increasing. Requesting emergency throttling guidance.

sophie: Seeing same. Prometheus alerts firing for nvml memory pressure. Some nodes in shard-3 report kernel reboots. :grimacing:

kevin: Is this hardware fault or scheduler pressure? Any recent deploys?

ajay: No deploys in the last 6 hours. Looks like a traffic surge from a single high-throughput customer (Mistral-Health-prod). Their recent load: ~6x baseline for long-context completions.

liz: If it's one customer, we should activate per-customer throttles first before region-wide measures. Can we restrict them to 1 concurrent session / 4r/s?

oncall-uk: I can apply a per-customer token bucket rule now. Would like explicit throttle values to avoid breaking SLAs for others.

ajay: Recommend emergency rule: Mistral-Health-prod -> max_tokens_per_minute=15000, concurrency=2, rate_limit=3r/s. Also temporarily disable large-context class for them.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-213 - eu-west1 GPU degradation. Runbook step: consider throttles, failover, and capacity bump.

kevin: I pushed a quick RBAC-based quota change:
```
redwoodctl quotas update --customer "mistral-health-prod" --rate 3 --concurrency 2 --window 60
```

liz: Applying prefix block for their 32k-context variants now (will route them to size-limited variants).

customer-eng: I messaged Mistral-Health support and asked them to reduce batch sizes; they're already rolling a patch to back off. They requested ETA ~10m.

ajay: Meanwhile, start gradual traffic shift for non-urgent EU traffic to us-west2 to relieve pressure. Policy: 20% -> 40% over 15m. Use smart routing to prefer cheaper model variants for background jobs.

kevin: Started canary traffic shift:
```
redwoodctl route update --from-region eu-west1 --to-region us-west2 --percent 20 --selector "background: true"
```
Alerts: queue length dropped 15% within 5m after initial shift.

sophie: GPU OOMs reduced but kernel restarts still happening on 3 nodes. Eng-runtime to patch and cordon those nodes.

kevin: Cordon + drain initiated on nodes gw-eu-3{7,9,11}. Scheduling new pods to other healthy nodes.

ops-bot: Autoscaler triggered: added 6 ephemeral GPUs to eu-west1 reserved pool (estimate: 8-12m to attach).

liz: We should also add a short-term region-wide emergency rate limit to protect critical customers while we stabilize. Proposal: global per-request token cost multiplier x2 for long sequences, and soft 25% reduction in per-customer burst allowances.

ajay: Agree. Apply global soft-limits and exempt customers with SLA-critical tag (apply manual overrides).

kevin: Implemented soft limits and exemptions. Saved snapshot of previous quota state to rollout rollback if needed.

customer-eng: Mistral-Health confirmed they reduced throughput by ~60% and long-context jobs stopped. They asked what the short-term limits were; I shared the values.

sophie: Monitoring: GPU util down to 70%, OOM alerts cleared, queue length trending down. Kernel restarts still under watch.

oncall-uk: We'll keep per-customer throttles in place for 4 hours and then re-evaluate. Ops: please add runbook note to suggest proactive quota warnings to customers when we see 3x baseline surges.

liz: Added runbook note and created a ticket to implement automated pre-throttle notifications.

ajay: Final ask: prepare a post-incident blameless summary with timeline, decisions (per-customer throttle + region shift + cordon + ephemeral capacity), and suggested mitigations (auto-prenotify, better per-customer anomaly detection, failover warm pools).

ops-bot: Incident #INC-2026-213 updated: status -> stabilizing. Next update in 2h or on any regression. :white_check_mark:
